card: A gerund (**дееприча́стие**) is a verb used as an adverb: it adds a second action by the same subject. Imperfective: the **они́** stem + **-я** (**чита́ют → чита́я**), *while reading*. Perfective: the past stem + **-в** (**прочита́л → прочита́в**), *having read*. **Чита́я кни́гу, он улыба́лся.** **Прочита́в письмо́, она́ запла́кала.**

sections.body: Gerunds join two actions of one person without **и** or **когда́**. They're common in writing and careful speech, and a few are everyday words: **мо́лча**, **сто́я**, **не спеша́**.

Examples
Meaning
rows: the **они́** stem + **-я** (**-а** after ж, ш, ч, щ)

sections.title: Time comes from the main verb
sections.body: A gerund has no tense of its own. Imperfective means *at the same time* as the main verb; perfective means *before* it: **Выходя́ из до́ма, я закры́л дверь.** **Вы́йдя из до́ма, я поверну́л нале́во.** Perfectives of the **идти́** family end in **-я**: **войдя́, вы́йдя, придя́**.

sections.title: Same subject only
sections.body: The gerund's doer must be the subject of the sentence. ~~Чита́я кни́гу, мне ста́ло ску́чно~~ is a famous error: the boredom isn't reading. Say **Чита́я кни́гу, я заскуча́л.**

sections.title: Verbs with no gerund
sections.body: Some imperfective verbs have no gerund: **писа́ть, пить, есть, ждать, мочь, бежа́ть**. Use a **когда́** clause instead: **Когда́ я писа́л письмо́, …**

mistakes.why: Perfective verbs form the gerund in **-в**.

mistakes.right: Когда́ я гуля́л по па́рку, начался́ дождь.
mistakes.why: The rain wasn't walking: a gerund needs the same subject as the main verb.

examples.en: He smiled as he read the book.
Having read the letter, she burst into tears.

examples.ru: Верну́вшись домо́й, я сра́зу лёг спать.
examples.en: When I got home, I went straight to bed.
